3.text: They would leave their wares on the shore and go away. The Chukchee,

4.text: would come afterwards, take the wares, and leave their equivalent in peltries,

5.note: footnote reference marker U+00B9 SUPERSCRIPT ONE, absent from mz text; restored per §2.10 (pairs with the opener on line 42).

6.text: Chukchee tradition relates the following regarding trade with America: —

7.text: “On the other side of the sea, in a large forest, live ‘the invisible ones.’
7.note: mz text mixed straight/curly quotes; corrected to the book's curly quotes throughout (§1, §5.6, keying_spec item 6) — outer double quote opens here, inner single quote around the embedded exclamation, both confirmed on the contact sheet for lines 7-14.

8.text: When they come to trade, one can see only the fox and beaver skins which

9.text: they carry in their hands, and it seems as if the peltries move of themselves.

10.text: They come to meet our traders on the border of the forest, and shout, ‘Let
10.note: mz keyed an opening double quote here; the sheet shows a single quote (curly), matching the embedded-speech convention closed on line 11.

11.text: us trade!’ The traders take a bundle of tobacco and fling it far away.

12.text: ‘Tobacco, tobacco!’ rings through the forest, but nobody is seen. After a

13.text: while a bag filled with fox or beaver skins is flung from the forest. For one,

14.text: bundle of tobacco they will give a bagful of white-fox skins.”

15.text: Some trade with the Koryak was also probably carried on before the

16.text: advent of the Russians. I heard that in the south of the Parapolsky Dol, on

17.text: the river Anapka, an ancient fair was held at which several camps of Reindeer

18.text: Koryak and Chukchee, of Maritime Chukchee, and even of Kamchadal, used

19.text: to gather. Perhaps a few articles of Japanese manufacture may have come

20.text: to the north in this way. At least, the question of the origin and manufacture

21.text: of Chukchee iron armor suggests a connection with the Japanese which does

22.note: footnote reference marker U+00B2 SUPERSCRIPT TWO, absent from mz text; restored per §2.10 (pairs with the opener on line 43).

23.text: This armor, made of small pieces of iron with fastenings of narrow leather

24.text: strips, was very common among the Reindeer Chukchee until recently. Even

25.text: now, many individuals preserve their armor out of reverence for its antiquity.

26.text: Besides armor, helmets and greaves were used, all of which are in some

27.text: degree similar to those of Japanese production. The Chukchee, however, are

28.text: not sufficiently skilled in the blacksmith’s art to forge such armor. The only

29.text: place where it could have been made is in the Koryak village of Poiˊtɪn
29.resolved: Poiˊtɪn = P, o, i, U+02CA MODIFIER LETTER ACUTE ACCENT (postposed stress), t, U+026A LATIN LETTER SMALL CAPITAL I, n
29.note: Koryak toponym (Tier-1 notation, keying_spec §2.1/§2.3). mz read this as ASCII "Poi'tin"; confirmed at 4x that the raised mark is the stress sort (never apostrophe by default, keying_spec item 8) and the final vowel before -n is small-cap ɪ, not dotted i — clear serif-top-and-bottom stem, no dot, contrasted against the dotted i in "village" on the same line.

30.text: (Russian Paren, Парень), the inhabitants of which have for a long time occupied

31.text: themselves with farriery; and the tradition of the southwestern Chukchee points

32.text: in this direction. The question arises, whether the manufacture of this armor

33.text: was really developed only after the arrival of the Russians, especially as the

34.text: wars have decreased since the last half of the eighteenth century.

35.text: Not less remarkable are the armor and helmet of Japanese make which

36.text: I acquired from a Reindeer Chukchee of the North Anadyr tundra. They

37.text: are old and rusty, and it was asserted that they had been in the family of

38.text: their owner for several generations. It is certain that in recent times no

39.text: Japanese traders have visited Anadyr Bay. The Japanese probably had some

40.text: intercourse with the southern Kamchadal. Steller and Krasheninnikoff mention
